author: MiniMax Agent
description: VORTEX-OS is a self-bootstrapping PowerShell skill that drives the .NET 10 C++/CLI engine at Cloudmeru/vortex-os-dotnet to orchestrate multi-agent work pipelines. The engine decomposes a master objective into a 4-tier chain of command (planner -> supervisor -> shift -> specialized workers), runs the workers in parallel across distinct domains, enforces continuity + contract rules, gates high-stakes actions behind Human-in-the-Loop approval, and writes a per-agent audit log. Engine v0.3.0+ adds a cross-project memory layer. Use it for multi-domain work, constraint enforcement across iterations, explicit HITL approval, per-agent audit trails, multi-iteration / series scope, and cross-project context reuse.

flow: User runs `pwsh -NoProfile -File skill.ps1 <args>` from the skill folder.
skill.ps1 searches $env:VORTEX_MODULE_PATH, $env:PSModulePath, and $HOME\Documents\PowerShell\Modules for an installed Vortex.<version>\Vortex.psd1.
If not found, skill.ps1 calls install.ps1, which downloads the 4 engine files from the public GitHub release of Cloudmeru/vortex-os-dotnet.
install.ps1 places the files in the first writable user-scope module folder (canonical: $HOME\Documents\PowerShell\Modules\Vortex\<version>\).
skill.ps1 sets $env:VORTEX_SKILL_ROOT to the skill folder so the engine finds agents/ + state/.
skill.ps1 imports the module and dispatches the command. Exit code from the engine is exposed via Get-VortexLastExitCode and used as the script's exit code.

name: VORTEX-OS

winget_install_ids.name: sqlite3
winget_install_ids.description: SQLite CLI (used by the engine's VectorHydrate for memory persistence). If missing, the engine skips memory persistence and writes a schema file instead.

winget_install_ids.name: ffmpeg
winget_install_ids.description: Audio/video processor. Not used by the engine itself, but required by generated *audio deliverables* (Foley, sample chopping, DSP). Install only if you plan to generate audio deliverables.

install_fallbacks.description: v0.2.3 (G10): if winget is not installed (older Windows, locked-down corporate machines, missing App Installer), install-deps.ps1 walks this list in order and uses the first one that exists. The 'direct' entry is a static URL the operator can paste into a browser; the script will also offer to download + unzip it.

requirements.winget_install_note: The engine is pure .NET 10 / C++/CLI. It does NOT need Python, jq, or any scripting runtime. All system deps install via Windows Package Manager (winget) — never pip/brew/apt. Use the bundled install-deps.ps1 to install. If winget is unavailable, the script falls back to choco, scoop, or a direct download (see install_fallbacks).

data_location.description: Starting with engine v0.1.7 + skill v0.1.4, the engine splits storage into a mutable skill folder and a durable VORTEX_HOME. The user's deliverables, audit log, swarms, and HITL state live in VORTEX_HOME so they survive skill updates and are shared across multiple skill instances on the same machine.
data_location.migration_strategy: manual via migrate-state.ps1 (not auto-migrated by the engine)

auto_update.description: Starting with skill v0.1.5, skill.ps1 checks for a newer vortex-os-dotnet release on GitHub on every invocation and installs it if available. Rate-limited to once per 6h per VORTEX_HOME.

do_not_use_when: Single-file edits with no cross-domain coordination
when_to_use: Building complex multi-disciplinary projects (research reports, software releases, data audits, design systems, media campaigns, interactive apps)
Managing multi-stage workflows across writing, audio, code, video, image, data, and research domains using native MiniMax engines
Automating multi-agent orchestration with constraint- or contract-bound outputs (brand guidelines, schema contracts, regulatory rules, design systems, code style)
Native Hailuo video generation and MiniMax image generation pipelines
Local ffmpeg audio processing, sample manipulation, and Foley synthesis
Internal app scaffolding — brainstorming, architecting, and coding complex digital environments for the MiniMax ecosystem
Long-running projects requiring constraint / contract enforcement across iterations (release trains, research programs, audit cycles, product lineups, episodic content)

Multi-step media production (tutorial video, ad cut, narrated slide deck, social clip): one source markdown / script → finished media with N slides, voiceover per slide, BGM, and a final MP4 cut (use the media-stack agent + media-tutorial-video recipe in `templates/`)

Multi-scene cinematic media (short film, narrative ad, brand story, product launch trailer, social short) that requires character continuity + palette consistency + cross-scene transitions across N short clips (Hailuo-2.3 caps at 10s/clip, H3 at 15s/clip; the director.cinematic agent produces a scene manifest + production bible and calls editor.stitch to assemble the final MP4 -- use the cinematic-short recipe in `templates/`)
Tasks requiring auditable decision-making with full audit trails
High-stakes deployments that need Human-in-the-Loop approval
Self-healing pipelines that recover from LLM drift
Cross-project context reuse (v0.3.0+ — per-project + per-series + per-operator memory so a new dispatch inherits the prior context)
Procedural media generation (audio, code, video, image, documents) at factory scale, entirely in-house with no external API keys

Quality-controlled media (auto-approve most worker outputs, retry the few that need regeneration, halt for human review only when something is truly wrong) -- the reviewer.quality agent calls the right per-template qa.* specialist and the --qa-threshold flag tunes strict/normal/loose

verification_status: v0.3.7 (skill-side reviewer.quality + per-template qa.* specialists): Two-layer QA architecture -- the framework (agents/reviewer.quality.json) picks the right per-template qa.* specialist and aggregates the verdict into one of three decisions (auto-approve / retry / hitl-halt). The specialists (qa.core for shared basic checks, qa.media-tutorial-video for slide coherence, qa.cinematic-short for character continuity + palette + voice + aspect, qa.iteration-pattern for the universal template) provide template-specific vision-LLM prompts + retry strategies. New --qa-threshold {strict|normal|loose} flag tunes the score threshold.
